title: fix(update): name the failure cause in generated reports without exposing private data
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated update failure reports hide actionable candidate startup causes and collapse config fields, leaving reports such as #178094 and #178244 difficult to triage.

Refs #178094, #178244, #145390.

## User Impact

Reports name recognized startup causes such as `plugin load failed: discord`, `port in use`, schema migration, native-module failures, readiness timeout, and process signals. Config errors retain schema vocabulary, for example `agents.entries.<id>.model.primary: expected string, got number`. Unknown plugin IDs, arbitrary keys, rejected values, and free-text diagnostics remain private.

## Why This Change Was Made

The #145390 allowlist is an intentional privacy boundary. The canary now records fixed facts before rolling logs or cleanup can obscure them, reusing the existing `candidate-startup-failed` code. One fixed condition/template table serves capture and public admission. Config projection uses the existing core-schema classifier and existing key-redaction owner. The report projects each fact once and reuses it for summary and detail. The report exporter injects schema classification into shared redaction, keeping the trusted PR wrapper import closure free of the config-schema graph. The phase summary retains existing allowlisted stderr facts before adding fixed producer facts.

The compression removes the standalone startup classifier, config adapter module, extracted type-only module, duplicate config/startup report projections, redundant code registration, and the second union-issue mapper. Existing canary types live beside the command type they describe; no new cause model or failure-fact shape is introduced. The existing private diagnostic contract remains intact.

## Evidence

The held-head CI failures were traced to three regressions: config projection treated the existing package field `engines.node` as an unknown config key; removing the free-text error-name bypass also lost fixed transaction/pipe causes; and shared redaction imported the config-schema lookup outside the trusted PR wrapper inventory. This revision restores the exact engine field and closed phrases (`attempt state write refused`, `sentinel transaction refused`, `sentinel transaction unavailable`, `pipe closed`) without restoring arbitrary prose. Schema projection is injected by the exporter. Both eager import-closure checks and the previously failing ordinary provisioning cases pass.

The consumer sweep also caught a structured startup fact displacing existing stderr facts. The new regression fails before the repair: `plugin load failed: discord` hides `EACCES; Permission denied`. Summaries now merge and deduplicate sanitized components within the existing 200-byte bound. The exact-template shortcut accepts only a single physical line, so it cannot discard later stderr lines.

The 55-file report/triage/wrapper consumer selection ran on both Node and Bun. The final focused Node replay passes **201 tests** across seven files, including the CLI runtime-fact handoff, campaign persistence/transfer failures, all public redaction cases, and the candidate startup cases. The final Bun sweep passes **1,033 tests**, with one platform skip and two failures: the inherited APFS timeout described below, and an exact startup expectation that still expected only the config field. That expectation now explicitly requires both the retained generic config fact and the schema path; all **16 startup cases pass on Node and Bun** after the update. Separately, all **151 report/redaction tests pass on both runtimes**.

Core types, strict scoped test types, lint and formatting on the changed files, `git diff --check`, and Madge (**0 cycles**) pass. The final isolated five-file review completed with **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. The earlier Node discovery failures from missing CommonJS fixture receipts and dropped fixed causes are resolved; the final targeted replay is green. Intermediate runs invalidated by source changes were discarded and the final proofs use a frozen source revision.

The existing CLI subprocess group passes all 21 tests on both runtimes (Node 124.52s, Bun 160.34s); its serial real-process/timeout fixtures account for the measured cost. The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory remains omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; no baseline, timeout, or assertion was weakened.

The UI failure is inherited from the CI merge base: `7a0c15b15693` intentionally retained header rename during reconnect, while the old test expected detachment. Main fixes that assertion in `80afbe1b7950116b6d55c557c7c7d4bc5fd01330`. This branch has no UI diff; the complete five-case file passes on both Node (25.99s) and Bun (21.13s). An initial setup attempt could not find Chromium under the isolated HOME; using the existing Playwright binary cache with fresh test profiles resolved setup without changing product code.

The worktree-local temp root initially made CommonJS triage fixture children inherit the repository's ESM package scope, causing eight missing receipt files. A minimal Node probe reproduced `require is not defined in ES module scope`; a private temp-root `package.json` with `type: commonjs` restores the same package scope as the usual OS temp directory. This is proof setup only, not a repository change.

The cold/warm APFS provisioning case has an inherited local timing failure: 161.430s on Node against its existing 120s limit. It runs six real wrapper invocations serially; the preceding single-invocation cases average 21.777s, so six already exceed 130s. Its test, fixture, and provisioner are unchanged from main. No timeout or assertion was relaxed. Bun reproduces the same unchanged local timeout at 150.426s.

Earlier compression validation: the 18-file consumer run passed **812 tests** and exposed three relocated-package fixture failures; those three cases now pass after enforcing the fixture's dependency boundary (6.82s wrapper, 5.85s test file). One existing platform case was skipped. All report, config, Gateway and canary cases passed, including **119 canary cases**, **86 config/report cases**, and **44 Gateway report cases**.

The new unterminated-stderr regression fails without the fix: a recognized plugin cause becomes `[redacted-diagnostic]`. Attaching the captured facts after pipe closure makes it pass. The original config/startup regressions also failed against the original producers. Privacy tests retain token, email, path, host/IP, credentialed URL, phone, dynamic-key and arbitrary-prose coverage.

Core types, strict scoped test types (with the repository's `allowJs` setting), lint, formatting on all 32 changed files, `git diff --check`, and Madge (**0 cycles**) pass. The first expanded temporary test config omitted `allowJs` and rejected existing `.mjs` imports; correcting that config resolved the setup error without source suppressions.

The earlier compression review at `9d51c9c8` completed 40 passes but returned **incomplete** because its file chunks omitted cross-file context; this is not a clean automated verdict. Its two P2 claims requested public schema projection inside the local config-fact producers. Both were rejected after tracing the complete path: local facts intentionally retain scrubbed concrete keys, and `update-failure-report-prepare.ts` schema-projects every affected key before either CLI or Gateway submission. The validator-to-public-report privacy tests cover that boundary. A separate full-context read-only review found no actionable issue. The GitHub review's unterminated-stderr finding is fixed and has a red/green regression.

The five build-dependent suites previously stopped before execution because compatibility discovery treated two sealed recovery bundles as shared runtime chunks. The build owner now excludes their canonical entrypoint paths using its existing independent-graph set. Genuine shared-graph ambiguity still throws. Both new regression cases fail before the fix; all **19 tests pass** after it (2.823s test time, 45.35s wrapper including compiled preparation).

**Size:** production **+371 / -128 (net +243)**, tests/support **+466 / -21**, docs **+7 / -0**, against `f7908148d72e52c7deeca5520e1dfa71fa0c2655`. The complete change removes **185 net production lines** from the earlier net +428 proposal. This CI repair adds **21 net production lines** to `9d51c9c8` while retaining the compression. The deleted adapter/classifier/type files account for 234 removed lines; the former report projection loses 90 lines, replaced by 49 lines sharing the existing fact projection.

<details>
<summary>Remaining production blocks and why they are required</summary>

Net +243 remains above the requested ~150 target. This accounts for every remaining production hunk, including mechanical moves and formatting; none adds a new config, CLI, dependency, or storage contract.

| Owner / diff | Remaining blocks |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/lib/bundled-plugin-source-utils.mts` +3/-0 and `bundled-plugin-build-entries.mjs` +3/-0 | A root without its own `.git` uses filesystem discovery. This prevents a staged candidate under a parent checkout from inheriting an empty parent `git ls-files` result and losing its plugin assets. |
| `scripts/lib/update-compat-chunks.mts` +7/-1 | Two canonical entrypoint imports and two entries in the existing independent-bundle set; array formatting accounts for the rest. Required to let the five real-runtime suites build while retaining ambiguity rejection. |
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-config-failure.ts` +10/-5 | Imports the shared fixed-kind formatter and existing concrete-path formatter; uses validator path segments instead of dropping the fixed issue kind. |
| `src/config/validation-issues.ts` +12/-8 | Extends the existing union-branch selector to ignore root-only type mismatches and recover the unique nested object error. Required for `model.primary` instead of the enclosing model union. Binding-specific selection remains unchanged. |
| `src/infra/update-candidate-canary-commands.ts` +32/-0 and `update-candidate-canary.ts` +62/-62 | Moves the 28 existing type lines plus four import/spacing lines beside the existing command type; no new types. Startup catch records the natural signal/timeout before teardown; fixed facts attach after the pipes close, preserving final unterminated diagnostics. The pending step replaces the former lint-only slot so cleanup warnings cannot displace its exactly-once receipt. The one-use cleanup wrapper is inlined; remaining edits are references and formatter changes. |
| `src/infra/update-candidate-canary-process.ts` +32/-1 | One bounded fact array; direct condition-table lookup at the existing stderr observer; fixed config field recognition after its heading; duplicate/bound checks; optional plugin identity capture; returns the same facts to the canary. No classifier pipeline or new state owner. |
| `src/infra/update-candidate-canary-readiness.ts` +5/-3 | Marks the three existing deadline failures with the standard `TimeoutError` name so the producer can distinguish timeouts from crashes. No new error class. |
| `src/infra/update-preflight-details.ts` +27/-0 | The single closed table covers the real config, schema migration/newer-schema, plugin, port, native ABI/missing-module, and fatal-memory envelopes. Patterns choose fixed text only; matched error prose never enters a public message. |
| `src/infra/update-failure-facts.ts` +23/-9 | Shares the fixed config grammar, preserves bounded field lines from admission protocol 1, and scrubs paths separately from fixed kinds. This avoids erasing `apiKey` diagnostics as apparent secret assignments on a second normalization pass. Unknown prose keeps the existing private-only redaction path. |
| `src/infra/update-failure-report-prepare.ts` +71/-29 | Loads the core schema once and supplies its segment classifier to redaction, including the exact package `engines.node` exception; projects each fact once; preserves the old sanitized aggregate before adding fixed field/message/plugin facts and deduplicates within 200 bytes. Distinguishes validator kinds from non-validation field errors; removes the duplicate renderer and error-name free-text bypass. |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-support-redaction.ts` +84/-10 | Reuses the existing path tokenizer and an injected segment classifier, keeping the schema outside the shared wrapper closure; projects schema-owned segments with `<id>`/`<key>` and retains the no-schema fallback. A closed validator-kind formatter/parser handles type, required and unrecognized-key issues, exposing only the known retired `approvalPolicy` key. Exact single-line startup templates and OS signals are admitted; the existing config-field branch uses the same parser. The closed cause list retains the four existing transaction/pipe phrases. |

</details>

The previously blocked built-runtime selection was the original 13-file report/canary selection plus these five files: `legacy-config-migrate.e2e.test.ts`, `config-startup-corpus.test.ts`, `update-candidate-canary.integration.test.ts`, `openshell-agent-workspace.e2e.test.ts`, and `required-native-same-session.e2e.test.ts`. Its real runtime preparation passed: tsdown 2m51.4s, external-plugin assets 13.4s, bootstrap guard 9.23s, copies 16.9s, runtime postbuild 13.7s. The first three suites passed; OpenShell is platform-skipped. The native-session suite started its isolated Gateway and installed the worker, then failed after 44.235s because workspace materialization rejects the worktree volume's inherited group-writable permissions. The trust check and mount permissions were not weakened.

The real built candidate integration passed in 65.481s, including snapshot preparation, Doctor/config/plugin/runtime checks, Gateway startup/readiness, and reaping the candidate while the preoccupied sandbox listener remained up. This is an existing full-flow test, not a unit test starting a real update per case. The existing test-plan suite repeatedly evaluates repository-wide selections; the final tooling shard took 221.5s. The CLI-process consumer group previously passed 21 tests in 162.86s, dominated by separate CLI boots. These measured costs remain recorded; no timeout was increased.

Two existing build collectors previously inherited an ancestor checkout for staged, unpacked roots. Both now require their own `.git` marker before using the Git inventory. A new nested-root regression fails without this guard. The no-scan tests permit only the exact root-marker probe and still reject every extension-directory scan. The three relocated grammar cases now reject dependencies resolved outside their copied package, retaining both the absent-native-grammar assertion and the real parse assertions.

The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory remains omitted under the campaign's local gate budget. PR CI is the broad authority. No baseline or timeout was increased and no test was skipped by this revision.

</details>
